name: GameSir Cyclone 2
_comment: Names are as printed on the pad: A B X Y, LB RB LT RT, VIEW (-), MENU (+), HOME (logo), L3/R3 (stick clicks). The D-pad is a hat on Linux. SHARE, M and the L4/R4 back paddles send nothing of their own - L4/R4 repeat whichever button you program onto them (hold M + L4/R4, press a button). Holding M + A for 2 s swaps A/B and X/Y, and the numbers also change with the connection mode (Home LED: green XInput, red Switch, yellow Android/HID; this pad also shows up as a DS4 'Wireless Controller' over Bluetooth). If presses land on the wrong action, re-run 'uv run map_controller.py gamesir_cyclone2' in the mode you actually use - it rewrites this OS's section from what the pad really sends.
_aliases: Extra names on top of the standard ones in controllers/__init__.py (L1=LB, START=MENU, ...).

linux._comment: Seeded from the kernel's order for the DS4-mode device (054c:05c4, hid-playstation): A=BTN_SOUTH, B=EAST, Y=NORTH, X=WEST, then TL TR TL2 TR2 SELECT START MODE THUMBL THUMBR. Overwritten by map_controller.py.

windows._comment: Seeded from SDL's standard XInput layout (the table in the README). The D-pad is buttons 11-14 and the triggers are axes 4/5, not buttons. Unverified on this pad - run map_controller.py on Windows to confirm.
